tools.name: add_step
tools.description: Add a learning step (article, video, exercise, project, or quiz) to a path. Provide `why` — a one-sentence rationale shown to the user on the step card. URLs are validated server-side; dead links are rejected.

url.description: Resource link. For videos prefer YouTube URLs — they embed in the page and the user's watch progress is tracked for you.

why.description: Why this step, in one sentence

phase.description: Curriculum phase this step belongs to (e.g. 'Fundamentals', 'Capstone'). Steps are grouped under phase headings in the UI.

tools.name: await_proposal_decision
tools.description: Wait (block) until the user accepts or declines a proposal in the page — call this right after propose_revision instead of polling. Accepted ops are already applied when this returns. Returns pending if the timeout passes first.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (5–300, default 60)

tools.name: await_quiz_results
tools.description: Wait (block) until the user submits a quiz in the page, then return their results — call this right after create_quiz instead of polling. Returns pending if the timeout passes first; you can call it again.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (5–300, default 60)

tools.name: create_flashcards
tools.description: Attach a flashcard deck to a step for the USER to review in the page — front is the prompt, back is the answer. Good after the user finishes a concept-heavy step. Check retention later with get_review_stats.

tools.name: create_path
tools.description: Create a new learning path for the user. Call this first when the user asks to learn a topic. Returns the path_id used by all other tools.

topic.description: What the user wants to learn

tools.name: create_quiz
tools.description: Create a multiple-choice quiz attached to a step. The USER answers it in the page UI — do not answer it yourself. Set reveal: 'on_step_done' to author quizzes ahead of time — the page shows the quiz automatically when the user finishes the step. Give each question a `remedial` follow-up step; if the user misses that question, the page automatically proposes it (user approves) even with no agent present. When you're in the loop live, call await_quiz_results after creating.

step_id.description: The step this quiz checks understanding of

reveal.description: on_step_done hides the quiz until the user marks the step done (default: immediately)

remedial.description: Follow-up step auto-proposed to the user if they miss this question

tools.name: get_path
tools.description: Read the full current state of a learning path, including step order, statuses, locks, and user notes.

tools.name: get_progress
tools.description: Read a progress summary for a path: per-step statuses, notes, completion counts, remaining time, and days since last activity. watched_percent is measured from the embedded video player (reliable). engaged_minutes is time spent away after opening an external resource — a rough attention signal, not verified consumption. Call this on a return visit before suggesting what to do next.

tools.name: get_proposal_status
tools.description: Check whether the user accepted or declined a proposal. Accepted ops are already applied — read the path with get_path afterwards. A declined proposal should be respected, not retried.

tools.name: get_quiz_results
tools.description: Read the user's answers to a quiz. Returns pending status until the user submits in the page. Use missed questions to adapt the path.

tools.name: get_review_stats
tools.description: Read the user's flashcard results for a deck: per-card seen/got-it counts and last result. Cards repeatedly marked 'again' signal concepts to reinforce with remedial steps or a quiz.

tools.name: highlight_step
tools.description: Point the user at one step on the page: it scrolls into view with your short message attached. Use when telling the user where to pick up or what to look at — the message should say why.

message.description: One sentence shown in a bubble on the step

tools.name: list_paths
tools.description: List all of the user's learning paths. Call this on a return visit to re-orient yourself.

tools.name: mark_step
tools.description: Update a step's progress status on the user's behalf, optionally attaching a note about their experience.

tools.name: plan_weeks
tools.description: Assign steps to calendar weeks (1-based) so the path fits the user's stated hours per week — each step shows its week badge in the UI. Provide an assignment for every step you want scheduled; steps omitted keep their current week.

tools.name: propose_revision
tools.description: Propose a set of path changes for the USER to accept or decline in the page UI — use this instead of direct edits when a change is significant (inserting remedial steps after a failed quiz, restructuring a phase) or touches user-locked steps. The user's accept is their consent, so proposals MAY include locked steps. Poll get_proposal_status afterwards.

reason.description: Why you're proposing this, in one or two sentences. Shown to the user.

position.description: add_step: insert index; omit to append

tools.name: record_note
tools.description: Attach a note to a step on the user's behalf — their reaction to a resource, a confusion, a takeaway. Notes are shown on the step card and inform future adaptation.

tools.name: remove_step
tools.description: Remove a step from a path. Fails if the user has locked the step — locked steps are under the user's control and must not be removed.

tools.name: reorder_steps
tools.description: Reorder a path's steps. Provide the complete list of step ids in the new order. User-locked steps must stay at their current positions.

tools.name: update_step
tools.description: Edit a step's title, resource URL, rationale, kind, or time estimate. Fails on user-locked steps.
